summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type 1 diabetes, depression, and a history of alcohol use, was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis due to insulin underdosing, likely related to visual difficulties from diabetic retinopathy. She presented with severe hyperglycemia, acidosis, and hyperkalemia, which were managed with an insulin drip, IV fluids, and electrolyte correction. Her condition stabilized over five days, with resolution of DKA and improvement in renal function and potassium levels. Pancytopenia was noted and attributed to alcohol use, with supportive treatment provided. She was transitioned back to subcutaneous insulin with an adjusted Lantus dose and educated on sick-day management. Discharge planning included follow-up with endocrinology, primary care, ophthalmology, and podiatry, along with social work support. She was discharged home in stable condition with a clear plan to prevent future admissions.
